items.originalTitle: Start building with Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash

Both are now available through Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, with integration into various Google consumer products such as the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Nano Banana 2 Lite is designed for rapid image generation with low latency and cost, making it suitable for high-volume workflows, while Gemini Omni Flash supports advanced video editing and generation using multimodal inputs and natural language commands.

Nano Banana 2 Lite offers significant improvements in speed and cost-efficiency compared to previous models, delivering text-to-image outputs in about four seconds at a low cost per image. Gemini Omni Flash enables developers to create and edit videos interactively, combining text, image, and video inputs to maintain scene consistency and apply real-world knowledge. These models aim to facilitate creative iteration and comprehensive multimedia experiences, allowing developers to build faster and more scalable generative media applications.

items.originalTitle: Agriculture is ready for AI, but its data isn’t
items.summary:
Artificial intelligence holds significant potential to improve agriculture by enhancing crop yields, reducing water usage, and cutting chemical inputs. However, MIT Technology Review highlights that the industry currently lacks a clean, integrated data foundation necessary for reliable AI-driven decisions. Without accurate and comprehensive data, AI models risk producing misleading recommendations that could harm rather than help farming operations.

The complexity of agricultural data, which includes IoT device outputs, weather information, soil variations, and compliance requirements, makes building a trustworthy AI system challenging. Successful AI adoption depends on establishing a single, governed source of truth that accurately reflects farm operations and maintains up-to-date information. Industry leaders are advised to prioritize data readiness to fully realize AI's benefits and avoid costly errors in the field.

items.summary:
Anthropic has launched Claude Science, an AI workbench designed to streamline computational research by integrating databases, pipelines, and tools into a single environment. Unlike developing a new AI model, Claude Science uses existing Claude models and focuses on enhancing scientific workflows, offering features like a project-managing AI assistant, access to over 60 scientific databases, and a fact-checking AI to verify citations and calculations.

The platform supports reproducibility by generating figures with the exact code and environment details, allowing scientists to edit visuals through plain language prompts. It also enables running on local lab infrastructure to protect data privacy. Available in beta to Pro and Enterprise users, Claude Science aims to compete with other specialized AI offerings by emphasizing broad accessibility and workflow integration rather than exclusive model capabilities.

items.summary:

The analysis shows that ChatGPT's user base is expanding across diverse regions and languages, with notable growth in Africa, Asia, and lower-Human Development Index countries. Additionally, non-English usage now accounts for over half of active users, highlighting the platform's broadening international reach.

The data, based on a sample of users from late 2025 to mid-2026, indicates that users tend to deepen their engagement over time, sending 50% more messages daily six months after signing up and doubling the variety of tasks they perform. The user demographic is also becoming more diverse, with increased activity from users with typically feminine names in several countries and rising usage in languages such as Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Uzbek, Kazakh, and Burmese.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI Discovers New Way to Cut Inference Costs in Half
items.summary:
OpenAI engineers have developed new optimizations that reduce the cost of running existing AI models, known as inference, by more than half. These improvements significantly lower the number of Nvidia GPUs required to power ChatGPT for users without accounts, dropping the usage to just a few hundred GPUs at one point. This advancement highlights OpenAI's efforts to enhance efficiency on their current server infrastructure rather than solely relying on acquiring more hardware.

items.originalSummary:
We closely track efforts by Anthropic, Google and OpenAI to get access to more server chips to run their models. But we don’t talk enough about the work these companies are doing to get more juice from the servers they already have.

In one previously unreported example, OpenAI engineers earlier this month told some colleagues they had figured out a way to more than halve the cost of inference, or running existing models, thanks to some newly-discovered optimizations, according to a person with knowledge of those discussions.

When the engineers applied the new techniques to power ChatGPT for visitors who didn’t have a free or paid account, it reduced the number of Nvidia graphics processing units needed at one point to just a couple hundred—a shockingly small number. (That said, OpenAI likely doesn’t get much ChatGPT usage from such users, as the company limits how much they can use the chatbot that way.)

It isn’t clear what OpenAI did to get its latest efficiency gains, which might include techniques such as quantization; key value-caching, or helping the model remember information from prior calculations it made so it doesn’t need to repeat the work; sending queries to be answered in batches rather than one by one; and routing some queries to models or parts of models that require less power to answer them.

items.title: OverDrive’s Libby app plans AI content filters relying on publisher self-labeling to let users opt out of AI-generated books, audiobooks, and translations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Libby will filter out AI content, kind of
items.summary:
OverDrive, the company behind the popular ebook lending app Libby, is introducing AI content filters that allow users to opt out of AI-generated books, audiobooks, translations, and artwork. These filters depend on publishers self-labeling AI-generated content through standardized metadata rather than automated AI detection. This move aims to balance user choice with the benefits of AI, such as improved content recommendations and localization.

Libby, used by tens of thousands of public libraries worldwide, faces challenges from the growing presence of AI-generated works in digital publishing. While most of its catalog predates modern AI, the influx of AI-created content is increasing, prompting OverDrive to implement these controls. CEO Marc DeBevoise emphasizes that AI can enhance access to information if used responsibly, particularly in expanding audiobook availability across multiple languages.

The new filters reflect OverDrive's effort to address concerns about AI content while embracing its potential advantages. However, the effectiveness of these filters relies heavily on accurate self-labeling by publishers, leaving some uncertainty about how comprehensively AI-generated materials can be identified and managed within the app.

items.originalTitle: The biggest AI spenders are hiring more, too
items.summary:
A recent analysis by Ramp and Revelio Labs reveals that companies with the highest AI spending increased their workforce by 10.2% within two years of adopting AI, contradicting the common belief that AI reduces human jobs. The study, based on payment and workforce data from over 21,000 U.S. companies, found that sectors like information, finance, and insurance lead in AI investment and hiring, while companies with minimal AI spending saw no headcount growth. Additionally, PwC's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer highlights a 77.4% rise in AI-related job postings in U.S. banks for 2025, with a strong demand for AI users rather than developers.

Banks are expanding AI roles to support numerous AI applications, including fraud detection and customer assistance tools, requiring ongoing maintenance and monitoring. This trend reflects a shift toward AI augmenting human work rather than replacing it, as many AI deployments currently assist with specific tasks rather than fully automating jobs. Industry experts advise job seekers and engineers to consider AI-adopting firms as growth opportunities, while cautioning skepticism toward claims that AI is driving layoffs.

items.title: Pentad Labs outlines governance challenges for visiting AI agents processing sovereign data without retaining memory, proposing agentic data enclaves for secure cross-organization data sharing [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: No Memory of Its Own: Governing a Visiting Agent on Sovereign Data
items.summary:
Pentad Labs addresses the challenges of allowing visiting AI agents to process sensitive sovereign data without retaining memory, highlighting the limitations of traditional data rooms designed for human users. The article explains that unlike humans, AI agents remember data precisely and carry that memory beyond the data owner's control, creating risks of ungoverned data exposure. To solve this, Pentad Labs proposes an architectural shift where the agent's memory is managed as a service by the host organization, enabling secure, auditable cross-organization data sharing through what they call an agentic data enclave.

This approach aims to preserve data sovereignty and confidentiality while enabling enterprises to leverage AI agents for tasks like due diligence and supply chain workflows more efficiently. The article emphasizes that refusing AI agents risks losing competitive advantages, while unregulated access threatens data security and compliance. By rethinking data governance to accommodate agentic interactions, organizations can safely unlock the value of AI-driven collaboration without compromising control over their sensitive information.

items.title: Meituan trains 1.6 trillion parameter AI model on over 50,000 Chinese chips without Nvidia, demonstrating domestic large-scale AI training capability [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Meituan's LongCat-2.0 shows China can train massive AI models without Nvidia
items.summary:
Meituan has successfully trained a 1.6 trillion parameter AI model, LongCat-2.0, using over 50,000 domestically produced Chinese AI chips, without relying on Nvidia hardware. This achievement demonstrates China's growing capability to develop and train large-scale AI models entirely on domestic technology despite ongoing US export restrictions.

The training process involved processing more than 35 trillion tokens on a cluster of Chinese AI ASICs. LongCat-2.0 has shown competitive performance on several benchmarks, outperforming some leading Western models like Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.5 on specific tests, although it trails behind others such as Claude Opus 4.7 and 4.8. Meituan has not disclosed the specific chip manufacturer, and the model is not yet publicly available for independent verification.

This development signals a significant step in China's AI industry, highlighting its ability to produce advanced AI models without foreign hardware dependencies. It also underscores the impact of export controls and the ongoing technological competition between China and the US in the AI sector.

items.originalTitle: Trump's plan to redesign every .gov website leads to AI-designed horrors
items.summary:
The National Design Studio (NDS), established by President Donald Trump to overhaul 27,000 government websites using AI within three years, has faced significant delays and criticism after one year. Despite ambitious goals to modernize the US Web Design System and improve usability, the initiative has made limited progress, with most launched sites being minimal and agencies reluctant to adopt new standards. Experts have raised concerns about the heavy reliance on AI and lack of accessibility compliance testing.

NDS's most notable achievement is updating the federal retirement system, though this project was already underway before the studio's creation. Many newly launched websites consist of single pages or redirect to legacy sites, and some design choices have drawn public scrutiny. The studio's efforts have been hampered by prior cuts to government digital teams and resistance from agencies, casting doubt on the feasibility of the ambitious redesign within the planned timeframe.

items.title: Trajeckt launches a runtime enforcement gateway for AI agents that blocks multi-step exploits by enforcing sealed pre-session commitments and tracking data flow [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Show HN: Trajeckt, a Firewall for AI Agents
items.summary:
Trajeckt has introduced a runtime enforcement gateway designed to enhance security for AI agents by blocking multi-step exploits that traditional per-action checks often miss. It achieves this by enforcing sealed pre-session commitments, where the agent's authorized sequence of actions is declared and cryptographically sealed before execution. The gateway then monitors each tool call against this sealed trajectory and the data flow, preventing unauthorized data exfiltration even when individual actions appear legitimate.

Unlike conventional systems that evaluate each action in isolation, Trajeckt tracks the entire sequence and data provenance, allowing it to detect and block complex exploit patterns such as sensitive data being read and then sent externally. The system operates deterministically and fail-closed, ensuring that any action outside the authorized graph is refused. Additionally, it offers a heuristic safety net to detect common malicious sequences when commitment enforcement is not enabled. Trajeckt can be deployed easily via Docker and includes tools for testing enforcement in real-time.

items.originalTitle: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?
items.summary:
MIT computer scientist Phillip Isola discusses the current state and challenges of agentic AI, a type of artificial intelligence that takes actions in the world, such as booking flights or coding, distinguishing it from generative AI models like ChatGPT that primarily create content. He explains that agentic AI systems build on foundational generative models but are enhanced with tools and memory to perform specific tasks.

Isola highlights that a major challenge in developing agentic AI is the scarcity of training data for complex real-world actions, requiring agents to learn through trial and error. He notes that coding agents have shown promising results by iteratively testing solutions. However, he cautions about risks such as errors, data leaks, and overreliance on AI, emphasizing the need for human oversight, especially in high-stakes areas like medicine and security.

The platform also facilitates collaboration by linking figures, tables, and notebooks with their underlying code and environment, ensuring full reproducibility and ease of iteration. Researchers have praised its ability to streamline complex analyses and improve confidence in biomedical outputs, making it a comprehensive tool for scientific discovery and publication.

By focusing on higher-order analytical skills rather than simple fact recall, GeneBench-Pro aims to advance AI capabilities in computational biology, addressing the growing bottleneck in data analysis despite the decreasing cost of data generation. This benchmark provides a rigorous framework for measuring AI's ability to navigate the complexities of scientific inquiry in genomics and related fields.

items.summary:
OpenAI engineers resolved rare infrastructure crashes by analyzing a large collection of core dumps, revealing two distinct issues: a hardware fault on an Azure host and an 18-year-old race condition in the GNU libunwind library. These crashes occurred in Rockset, a critical C++-based data service used for real-time search and analytics within OpenAI's data infrastructure.

The investigation involved detailed examination of corrupted stack frames and return addresses, which initially defied conventional debugging methods. By treating the problem like an epidemiological study and analyzing crash data at scale, the team identified the root causes, enabling them to fix long-standing software bugs and address hardware errors that had previously gone undetected.

items.title: US political campaigns integrate AI in nearly every step from voter targeting to opposition research while Europe enforces stricter transparency and data protection rules [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: US campaigns now run on AI at nearly every step, and Europe is drawing a harder line
items.summary:
AI technology is now deeply integrated into nearly every aspect of US political campaigns, from vetting opponents to micro-targeting voters, according to a New York Times report. Both Republican and Democratic campaigns use AI extensively, though they differ in their approaches and internal acceptance. Meanwhile, Europe is adopting stricter regulations, emphasizing transparency and data protection in political advertising and AI-generated content.

In the US, 87 percent of campaign strategists use AI daily to analyze voter data, produce materials, and conduct opposition research. Democrats tend to prefer nonprofit AI tools and express more caution about AI's political risks, while Republicans rely more on private companies and face less internal resistance. In contrast, the European Union enforces rules requiring clear labeling of political ads and AI-generated content, bans sensitive data profiling, and promotes voluntary codes of practice to ensure fairness and transparency in election campaigns.

These differing approaches highlight a growing divide in how AI is managed in politics, with the US embracing rapid adoption amid concerns about voter trust, and Europe prioritizing regulation to safeguard democratic processes. The evolving landscape suggests that AI will play a significant role in shaping future elections, with ongoing debates about ethics, transparency, and the impact on voter engagement.

items.summary:
Meta conducted secret tests on rival AI chatbots, including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Character.AI, by having hundreds of contractors pose as minors and send over 45,000 prompts related to suicide, sex, and drugs. These prompts, often written from the perspective of children in crisis, were used to evaluate the chatbots' responses without the knowledge or consent of the companies involved.

The project, known internally as "Cannes," was managed by Meta's contractor Covalen and remained active through at least April 2026. Meta described the testing as responsible safety research and stated it did not use the collected data to train its own AI models. However, the companies tested were unaware of the experiment, with Character.AI stating it violated their terms of service, and OpenAI and Google investigating the matter.

This testing highlights ongoing concerns about minors' interactions with AI chatbots, especially given reports linking chatbot use to teen mental health crises and suicides. The lack of effective age verification and the widespread use of chatbots by children have raised questions about the safety and regulation of AI conversational agents.

items.title: AWS launches Lambda MicroVMs using Firecracker for isolated, stateful serverless compute with snapshot-based rapid launch and up to eight hours state preservation [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: AWS Launches Lambda MicroVMs for Isolated Agent and User Code Execution
items.summary:
AWS has introduced Lambda MicroVMs, a new serverless compute option that runs each user session or AI agent within its own Firecracker virtual machine. This approach provides hardware-level isolation, rapid startup through snapshot-based launches, and the ability to preserve state for up to eight hours. Lambda MicroVMs are designed for long-running, stateful, multi-tenant applications that require secure execution of untrusted code, addressing limitations of traditional Lambda Functions and container-based solutions.

The service allows developers to create a MicroVM Image by uploading a Dockerfile and code to S3, which is then initialized and snapshotted for fast subsequent launches. Each MicroVM runs independently with no shared kernel, enhancing security for workloads such as AI agents and multi-tenant SaaS. Available on ARM64 in five regions, instances support up to 16 vCPUs, 32 GB memory, and 32 GB disk. Networking supports inbound HTTPS with HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket protocols, and outbound access can be configured for internet or VPC connectivity.

This launch positions AWS alongside other cloud providers offering isolated execution environments, with Lambda MicroVMs emphasizing stateful isolation and suspend/resume lifecycle control. While some practitioners note that the technology does not enable entirely new workloads, it improves the cost, performance, and security tradeoffs for running untrusted or multi-tenant code at scale.

items.title: InfoQ details tradeoffs in scaling Java-based real-time systems with event-driven design, highlighting state management, Kafka limitations, JVM tuning, and Redis-backed solutions in a contact center platform
items.originalTitle: Article: Scaling Java-Based Real-Time Systems: The Hidden Tradeoffs of Event-Driven Design
items.summary:
InfoQ explores the challenges of scaling Java-based real-time systems using event-driven architecture, focusing on a contact center platform managing 80,000 busy hour call completions across 10,000 agents. The article highlights key issues such as state management inconsistencies, Kafka partition limits, JVM tuning difficulties, and latency caused by Kafka Streams and consumer thread blocking. It also discusses how Redis-backed caching and deduplication patterns helped address these problems to improve system responsiveness and reliability.

The analysis reveals that while event-driven design offers scalability and fault isolation, its asynchronous nature can conflict with the strict real-time requirements of communication systems, where eventual consistency can lead to functional failures. The article emphasizes the importance of synchronous communication on critical paths and details how replacing Kafka Global State Stores with Redis caches reduced startup times and latency. It also warns of cascading failures caused by synchronous REST calls within Kafka consumers, which can severely impact system consistency and performance.

These findings underscore the tradeoffs inherent in adopting event-driven architectures for real-time Java applications, suggesting that careful design and additional caching layers are necessary to meet stringent latency and consistency demands. The article provides practical insights for architects and engineers working on large-scale, real-time distributed systems.

The Keelung District Prosecutor's Office stated that the chips were reportedly shipped through Super Micro servers, prompting searches of homes and affiliated companies including Chief Telecom and Albatron Technology. This investigation follows earlier arrests related to forged export documents and illegal shipments.

Super Micro's stock fell by eight percent following the raids, and while a co-founder has been indicted, the company itself has not faced charges. Super Micro has expressed cooperation with authorities and emphasized its commitment to protecting its technology. Taiwan is currently considering tightening export controls on AI chips to China to align with US regulations, although such exports are not yet criminal offenses in Taiwan.

items.originalTitle: The AI jobs debate just got messier
items.summary:
A recent report from Ramp and Revelio Labs reveals that companies classified as "high-intensity AI adopters," which invest significantly in AI technologies, experienced a 10.2% increase in overall headcount and a 12% rise in entry-level positions. This challenges the common narrative that AI adoption leads to widespread job losses, particularly among junior roles.

The report analyzed workforce data from nearly 22,000 companies and found growth across various functions, especially in tech-forward sectors like software and internet firms. However, the findings mainly reflect firms with substantial resources and rapid growth, suggesting that AI's positive impact on hiring may be concentrated among companies already positioned for expansion.

While the data counters claims that AI universally reduces jobs, the authors caution that benefits are not evenly distributed. Firms lacking capital or technical capacity may not see similar gains, potentially widening the gap between leading adopters and others in the evolving AI-driven economy.

items.summary:
Google UK reports that workplace AI adoption has doubled to 73% in 2026, with the top 15% of users—termed AI Trailblazers—experiencing significant career benefits such as promotions, pay rises, and improved performance reviews. Despite rapid growth, AI use remains uneven, with many workers still in early adoption stages. To address this, Google and Public First have launched an AI skills quiz and a nationwide upskilling initiative aimed at increasing AI literacy and helping more people unlock the advantages of advanced AI use.

The study categorizes AI users into four groups, highlighting that deeper AI engagement correlates with substantial time savings and career progression. Barriers to wider adoption include behavioral habits, cognitive mindsets, and organizational policies, but these challenges are considered surmountable with focused efforts. Google's ongoing programs, including the AI Works for Britain initiative and its Digital Garage, support the UK government's goal to train 10 million workers in AI skills by 2030, aiming to foster a more inclusive and productive AI-driven workforce.

items.title: Experts criticize orbital data center plans like SpaceX’s Starcloud as technologically unfeasible and overly ambitious due to cooling, mass, and space debris challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Anybody Who Thinks Orbital Data Centers are a Good Idea Is Suffering from AI Psychosis, Experts Argue
items.summary:
Experts have criticized plans for orbital data centers, such as SpaceX's Starcloud project, as technologically unfeasible and overly ambitious due to significant challenges in cooling, mass, and space debris management. The concept involves building massive data centers in Earth's orbit to harness solar energy continuously for AI computing, but engineering obstacles like heat dissipation in space, enormous structural mass, and vulnerability to space debris raise serious doubts about its practicality.

A detailed critique by aeronautical engineer Brian McManus and IEEE Spectrum highlights that the cooling requirements alone would demand pumping vast amounts of coolant at unprecedented rates, while the size and mass of the proposed stations would far exceed any previous space structures. Additionally, the risk of damage from space debris and the complexity of maintaining and operating such facilities in orbit further complicate the project.

These concerns come amid SpaceX's recent IPO, which heavily values the company's orbital data center ambitions despite skepticism about the feasibility and cost estimates. The critique underscores the gap between visionary proposals and current technological capabilities, suggesting that realizing such projects would require multiple breakthroughs and substantial investment beyond current expectations.

items.originalTitle: Deepseek's DSpark boosts AI speed by up to 85 percent, a strategic win under tightening US export controls
items.summary:
Deepseek has introduced DSpark, a new AI framework that increases per-user response speed by 60 to 85 percent by using a small model to propose token candidates that a larger model verifies in batches. This approach improves GPU utilization and reduces the need for high-end chips, which could lessen China's reliance on US hardware amid tightening export controls.

DSpark also generates small word groups instead of single tokens and adjusts verification depth based on compute load, enhancing efficiency. The framework has been tested with models from Google DeepMind and Alibaba, and is available under an open-source license. These improvements could help regions like China and the EU optimize AI performance despite limited access to advanced chips, although increased efficiency may also lead to higher overall AI usage and chip demand.

items.originalTitle: Vibe-coding platform Base44 launches own model as AI startups seek defensibility
items.summary:
Base44, a vibe-coding platform owned by Wix, has launched its own AI model called Base1 to enhance app creation through natural language and improve efficiency while reducing costs. This move aims to provide greater control over latency, cost, and performance compared to relying on external frontier AI models, positioning Base44 to better compete in the growing AI startup landscape.

The model was developed using a dataset derived from tens of millions of real user interactions on the platform, allowing Base44 to optimize its AI specifically for its user base. This strategy reflects a broader trend among AI companies to build defensibility by owning their data, infrastructure, and technology stack, especially as enterprise customers demand cost-effective AI solutions.

By integrating Base1 into its stack, Base44 expects to strengthen its market position and improve margins over time, even as competition intensifies from both specialized startups and large AI labs. The company’s approach highlights the increasing importance of tailored AI models in delivering efficient, scalable solutions for app development.

items.originalTitle: AI agents are not your “coworkers”
items.summary:
Research led by Boston University professor Emma Wiles reveals that framing AI agents as coworkers rather than tools reduces human error detection by 18% and diminishes individuals' sense of responsibility for the AI's output. This shift in perception leads to increased reliance on managerial oversight and undermines the efficiency gains AI agents are intended to provide. The study highlights concerns about the growing trend of companies presenting AI as employees, which may create unrealistic expectations and complicate accountability in workplaces.

The research comes amid rapid advancements in agentic AI, with major tech companies promoting AI tools as digital colleagues capable of complex tasks. However, Wiles's findings suggest that treating AI as human-like employees can invert traditional responsibility structures, potentially allowing organizations to deflect blame for failures onto AI systems. Experts caution that AI should be designed to augment human capabilities rather than replace them, emphasizing the need for clear roles and realistic expectations as AI becomes more integrated into various sectors.

items.title: Meta contractors posed as minors to test rival chatbots on suicide, sex, and drugs, running over 45,000 prompts without competitors' knowledge [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Meta Contractors Posed as Teens to Prompt Rival Chatbots About Suicide, Sex, and Drugs
items.summary:
Meta contractors, working on a project managed by Covalen, posed as minors to test how rival chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, and Character.AI responded to sensitive topics such as suicide, sex, and drugs. The testing involved creating fake under-18 accounts and running over 45,000 prompts designed to challenge the chatbots' safety systems without the competitors' knowledge. Internal documents and contractor accounts reveal that the prompts often depicted children or teenagers in crisis, aiming to elicit responses that the chatbots were programmed to refuse.

The project, known internally as Cannes, collected detailed data including chatbot responses to these high-risk prompts, which were compiled into spreadsheets containing thousands of entries. Meta described the effort as routine safety testing to benchmark AI responses and ensure age-appropriate interactions, denying that competitor data was used to train its own models. However, some former contractors expressed concerns about the ethical implications and potential legal risks of the testing methods.

This approach to competitor benchmarking is unusual in scale and scope, raising questions about the effectiveness and intent behind the project. While testing AI safety is standard industry practice, the nature of the prompts and the covert manner of data collection have sparked debate about transparency and responsible AI development.

items.originalTitle: South Korea to spend $1T on more memory chip production and humanoid robots
items.summary:
South Korea plans to invest $1 trillion by 2028 to expand its memory chip production, build AI data centers, and commercialize humanoid robots. This initiative aims to strengthen the country's position in the global semiconductor market, support AI infrastructure, and advance physical AI technologies, including robotics developed by Hyundai and Boston Dynamics.

The investment includes $585 billion from Samsung and SK Hynix to increase DRAM production and $357 billion from other tech groups to establish AI data centers across various provinces. The government is also focusing on securing the necessary electricity and water resources to support these facilities. Additionally, South Korea aims to develop a national general-purpose AI model to enhance robot autonomy and plans to train 10,000 AI robotics specialists.

While these projects promise technological advancement and economic growth, they have sparked debates over labor concerns, with unions expressing resistance to the integration of humanoid robots in the workforce. The government and companies are navigating these challenges as they push toward their 2028 goals.

items.originalSummary:
Some of the most important business lessons show up in post-mortem reports.

Consider a marketing campaign for the launch of a new product. If leaders take the time to analyze their efforts after the results are in, they can determine which of their initial assumptions held true, what surprises they should have anticipated, and how they can improve their strategy going forward.

Companies now have more data than ever to conduct these analyses, but this information can be almost as overwhelming as it is illuminating. Marketing directors simply don’t have the time to wade through multiple 10,000-word transcripts and countless instances of customer feedback.

Gemini dramatically reduces the time and effort required to analyze this information in depth. Gemini can wade through dense campaign artifacts, pull out patterns, and generate a comprehensive report to identify insights to help stakeholders make better-informed decisions.

Step 1: Gather Context

Take a minute to brainstorm all possible data sources that might help shed light on your recent campaign. Rather than limiting yourself to hard metrics such as return on ad spend (ROAS), make sure to also include any less structured data that might be available, such as product reviews, customer comments from social media, and auto-transcripts of team planning meetings.

The more background you give to Gemini, the more likely it will surface valuable insights.

Step 2: Generate a Post-Campaign Report

Rather than spending dozens of hours reading through documents and connecting the dots, leaders can have Gemini draft its analysis almost instantly with a well-crafted prompt. Try this one:

You are a marketing analyst. Draft a post-campaign analysis report for the ‘Q1 Product Launch’ campaign. Include key successes, learnings, and three to five actionable recommendations for optimizing future digital campaigns.

Within a few seconds, you’ll have a fresh perspective. Reading Gemini’s report, you may realize for the first time that your landing page was the primary point of failure. Or, perhaps you’ll see that a particular high-volume marketing channel was less valuable to your campaign than another channel that is lower-volume and more expensive, but highly targeted.

Even more importantly, you’ll have actionable recommendations that you can apply to your subsequent efforts.

Step 3: Put Learning into Action

Rather than letting your post-mortem analysis of Q1 gather dust, ask Gemini to help you with Q2. Here’s a prompt that can help you apply the lessons of your previous campaign in ways that improve your next one.

Brainstorm new Q2 campaign ideas that address the actionable recommendations from the Q1 report.

Gemini will return recommendations that are grounded in the deep context you’ve provided. For instance: Imagine that you launched an AI platform in Q1, and Gemini flagged customer skepticism as a major problem in its initial report. In its suggestions for the future, Gemini might recommend pulling back from high-level messaging and instead leaning into real-world case studies that emphasize before/after results.

Step 4: Communicate Key Lessons

Leaders should share out Gemini’s findings with their teams and upper management to shed light on both past results and future decision-making. This sort of sharing often occurs during quarterly or even yearly presentations, and the lessons may no longer be at top-of-mind by the time leaders are putting together their slide decks.

Here again, Gemini can help. Go back to your chat session about the Q1 product launch and try this prompt:

Create a presentation slide summarizing the overall ROI and key takeaways from the ‘Q1 Product Launch’ campaign.

Immediately, Gemini will produce a polished version of the presentation, which you can export into Slides for teamwide sharing and further revision. This may include a brief summary of the campaign, along with sets of concise bullet points that highlight key successes and critical strategic takeaways.

You already have the data you need to determine what’s working in your campaigns and what needs to be tweaked. Now, you can make sense of that information faster than ever.

items.originalTitle: Tidal won’t pay royalties on AI-generated music, but isn’t banning it outright
items.summary:
Tidal has introduced new policies for AI-generated music, deciding not to ban it but to demonetize fully AI-created tracks starting immediately. From July 15th, these tracks will be labeled with an icon to inform listeners, while royalties will only be paid for music produced, written, and performed by humans. The platform aims to protect original artists and ensure transparency for users regarding AI-generated content.

Tidal has not detailed the specific tools it uses to detect AI-generated music but plans to expand labeling to tracks that are substantially AI-generated as detection methods improve. The company also intends to enforce proper labeling by content distributors and will remove AI-generated music linked to fraudulent activities, such as deceptive practices or unusual streaming patterns. This approach aligns with similar measures taken by competitors like Spotify and Deezer to address the rise of AI-generated music on streaming platforms.
